chunks: Muhammad ibn Ali ibn Mahbub from Muhammad ibn al-Jabbar from al-Asfwan from Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Hajjaj said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about completing the prayer in Mecca and Medina. He said: Complete it, even if you have not prayed in them except one prayer.

key_terms.الإِتْمَام: Completing the prayer (praying four rak'ahs instead of two) while traveling
key_terms.وَالْمَدِينَةَ: And Medina, the other major holy sanctuary

ai.seo_question: Do I need to shorten my prayer if I prayed full prayer in Mecca or Medina?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Al-Istibsar* clarifies the ruling of *Salat al-Tamam* (full prayer) for travelers, establishing that performing a single full four-rak'ah prayer in the holy sanctuaries of Mecca or Medina grants the traveler the status of a resident for subsequent prayers. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) confirms that even if only one prayer was offered in full, the traveler is exempt from shortening (*Qasr*) for the remainder of their journey, highlighting the sanctity of these locations in Shia jurisprudence.
